t:
(a) GAO Report.—Not more than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall transmit to the Committee on Science of the House of Representatives and the Committee of Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report describing action taken by NASA to implement the recommendations contained in the Government Accountability Office’s Report No. 04–639. 
    (b) Compliance.—To comply with title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.), the Administrator shall conduct compliance reviews of at least 2 grantees annually.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a formal report and compliance reviews of grantees amount to outside involvement. The report goes only to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. The Title IX compliance reviews are federal oversight of grantees, not consultation with them before a federal decision. Nothing provides for public comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: the Administrator shall transmit to the Committee on Science of the House of Representatives and the Committee of Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report

opus.w: Subsection (a) requires a report to congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so this is not participation. Subsection (b) requires compliance reviews of grantees. That is the agency enforcing rules on outside parties, not consulting them before a decision. No public comment, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: the Administrator shall transmit to the Committee on Science of the House of Representatives and the Committee of Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **No**.

**The tempting misreadings:**
- Subsection (a) has a formal report, which can look like participation. But the report goes to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government.
- Subsection (b) brings in outside parties: the grantees. But the Administrator is checking whether they follow Title IX. The grantees are being reviewed, not giving input on a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Administrator to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation. The mention of compliance reviews of grantees describes an internal enforcement/audit activity, not a consultative process where outside parties influence a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: the Administrator shall transmit to the Committee on Science of the House of Representatives and the Committee of Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "compliance reviews" of grantees involve interaction with outside parties (the grantees), thus constituting participation. However, a compliance review is an internal audit or enforcement mechanism conducted by the agency to ensure rules are followed; it is not a process where the outside party consults with or advises the government on a decision. The primary action in this section is the transmission of a report to Congress.
